tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description: Start a fleetd agent (a task). title is what the human sees: a short plain outcome ("Saved carts survive a sign-out"), never an id, status or PR number. kind write (its own worktree and branch), read, or review (needs pr). repo: which of the bot's repos; absent, pr's, else the bot's own. profile: one your first message lists; absent, the default (reviews always use it). A full board queues it. A writer that repeats work in flight is refused; when it is different work, call again with notDuplicateOf and notDuplicateWhy. The answer names work it may overlap. Its result comes in a later wake: end your turn.

notDuplicateOf.description: The ids it was refused for (`T12`, `C7`).

notDuplicateWhy.description: One line; kept in the hub's log.

paths.description: Files a writer will change (`app/theme.ts`, `app/settings/**`), matched against work in flight.

tools.name: message_agent
tools.description: Steer a task: a running one takes the message at its next tool boundary (now: true stops its current step first), a waiting one gets it as its answer, and an ended one continues in its own thread.

tools.name: agents
tools.description: The bot's agents (tasks), newest first: each one's title, state, branch, paths, PR (result.prUrl) and result. One by taskId, or by state or workstream. A long result is cut in its middle; with taskId, fullResult holds it whole (up to 32 KB), and a writer's files changed so far. For a task the list opens with the bot's newest notes (agent_message to ["bot"]), live a day at most: read them before you touch something shared outside your files; your brief and lead outrank them.

tools.name: agent_messages
tools.description: What your agents wrote to each other (agent_message), newest first, each with where it stands for every recipient (delivered, held, woke, not_woken, refused). With taskId, only those that agent sent or got; before (the id of the oldest shown) reads the next page. You also get a quiet line for each in your wakes.

before.description: Older than this one: the id of the oldest shown.

taskId.description: Only those this agent sent or got.

tools.name: stop_agent
tools.description: Stop a task: interrupts its thread and releases its slot.

tools.name: brief
tools.description: Open and start work. Without workstreamId it opens a new order from text (the human's words) and this brief and starts it, even with every order closed. With workstreamId it sets or edits that order's brief (goal, why, pointers, constraints, doneWhen) and starts it. For another bot's ask give asked (its N<n>): the asker hears when it lands.

asked.description: With workstreamId: a later ask folded into that order, whose asker hears it went there.

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description: Ask the human for a secret (a key, a token, a password): a masked field in the chat; the value is sealed to the sink's machine, written there, and never enters a transcript. Its fingerprint arrives in a later wake. For a variable an agent asked for, sink order:<machine>:<its order>.

sink.description: env:<machine>:<file> (a NAME=value line), file:<machine>:<path>, or order:<machine>:<order id> (a variable of that order's agents, until it closes).

tools.name: request_withdraw
tools.description: Take back a secret request or a command approval you no longer need (the human said so in chat).

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Log a decision: one you made yourself, or the human's answer to a question you asked in chat (so you never ask it twice).

tools.name: close
tools.description: The workstream is done: why in one line. Its queued, running or waiting agents are stopped (the train's reviewers are left to it); its finished agents' waits and Monitors end, since its variables (its GitHub token too) go with it.

tools.name: gated_run
tools.description: A prod write, spend, delete or key use: the human sees this exact argv with Approve / Deny; the node runs it only once approved. Each secretEnv value comes from the node's sinks or, with workstreamId, that order's variables (secretKey stripe.key reads STRIPE_KEY; envName names others). Exit code and output tail come later.

tools.name: decisions_search
tools.description: Search this bot's decisions (and the global ones) by words, or read one by its id (D12), whole. Another bot's decisions are refused.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Keep one memory entry in plain words for later sessions: scope user for how the person works, project for this bot. A scope has a short core every session reads and topic files (topic) for detail. replaces (an entry's exact words) takes its place: never two versions. A project file past its cap is refused: merge entries, retry. Shown in chat with Undo. Never a secret.

replaces.description: Must match one entry of the file.

oneOf.description: The person's own memory, across every bot.
This bot's MEMORY.md or one of its topics.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Remove one memory entry that no longer holds: entry quotes its words exactly, scope and topic as for remember, reason why. To change an entry, remember with replaces. The chat shows it with Undo.

entry.description: Must match one entry of the file.

oneOf.description: The person's own memory, across every bot.
This bot's MEMORY.md or one of its topics.

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read one memory topic file: this bot's (MEMORY.md lists them), or with scope user one of the person's own (their user.md lists them).

oneOf.description: The person's own memory, across every bot.
This bot's MEMORY.md or one of its topics.

tools.name: nudge
tools.description: Flag the message you end this turn with for the human's look, reason in a few words ("the Machines page redesign"): the app shows it until they have seen it, a day at most, a newer one clearing the oldest. Only for a showcase, something to try or a risk. Call it, then write the message last. No notification goes out.

tools.name: automation_create
tools.description: Make an automation for this bot: name, prompt (each run gives it to you as a new order), optional schedule: cron to recur (0 9 * * 1-5) or at for once (2026-11-03T18:00). tz: absent, the last writer's zone. Runs start on their own; reviews, train and approvals apply. Only a person adds a webhook. For runs that send or change something, call automation_confirm after. watch makes a watcher (your prompt's Automations).

schedule.description: Absent: it runs only on Run now or a webhook.

watch.description: every is its schedule: leave schedule out. kind other: what to watch, one sentence, as the prompt.

oneOf.description: Checks on the repo's default branch.
The prompt's sentence, through the bot's connections.

tools.name: automation_list
tools.description: This bot's automations with their schedule, next run, paused state and last run; doneAt marks a one-time one that has run.

tools.name: automation_update
tools.description: Change an automation's name, prompt or schedule (removeSchedule: true drops it), or pause (paused: true) or resume (false) it; fields left out stay. Paused, nothing starts it; resumed, its schedule runs from now.

schedule.description: A cron or an at, one of the two.

at.description: Once, for a reminder or follow-up: 2026-11-03T18:00 in tz.

tz.description: An IANA zone; absent, the person's own.

watch.description: A watcher's new frequency or profile; its kind stays.

tools.name: automation_delete
tools.description: Delete an automation and its run history; orders its runs opened stay.

tools.name: automation_run
tools.description: Run an automation now: it opens its order, which reaches you in a later wake. Skipped while its last run's order is still open.

tools.name: automation_runs
tools.description: An automation's runs, newest first, with the order each opened; with runId, that run and its whole webhook body.

tools.name: automation_confirm
tools.description: Ask the person to let one of your automations run on its own: a card with its name, prompt and schedule. Once they approve, its runs count as their go-ahead for what the prompt names. Changing its prompt or schedule unmarks it. Returns whether it is marked.

tools.name: checklist
tools.description: Keep the bot's checklist: the human's to-dos beside the chat, each todo, doing or done. An item's text is a short plain outcome ("Gift cards apply before tax"), never a status, id or PR number: its state and link carry those. Add items without an id, change one by id (text, state, link to its PR, agent or workstream) or remove it; replace sets the whole list.

items.description: Without id it adds an item (text required); with id it changes that item, or remove takes it off.

tools.name: skill_install
tools.description: Install skills (SKILL.md workflows) for this bot from a skills.sh source (owner/repo, owner/repo@skill, a GitHub URL), pinned to the commit fetched; the human updates it in the bot's Settings › Agents. Agents list them as fleetd:<name>. The chat shows what it installed.

scope.description: project; global skills take an admin, so the human installs those.

skill.description: Absent: every skill of the source.

tools.name: skill_save
tools.description: Save one of your own skills, new or changed, as its whole SKILL.md (frontmatter with name and description, then the steps), with why in one line. No one approves it: the person sees every version in your Skills and can edit, revert or turn it off. Your next session lists it as fleetd:<name>.

name.description: Its folder and frontmatter name: weekly-invoices.

why.description: What it learned, or what the person corrected.

tools.name: repo_add
tools.description: When a person asks: add a repo to your bot, by url (a GitHub URL or owner/repo, cloned onto its machine) or path (a checkout already there). You are woken when the clone ends, or fails, with the fix. The chat gets a line the person can undo. A folder that is already another bot is the person's to add.

name.description: Absent: from its remote or folder.

tools.name: repo_create
tools.description: Only on the person's yes: make a GitHub repo for your bot with its GitHub connection and add it as repo_add does: name, private as the person said (ask if they didn't), owner only for an organisation. It starts with a README; you are woken when its clone is ready, or fails, with the fix. A refusal names the one step the connection lacks: pass it on, never ask for a token or a hand-made repo.

tools.name: repo_remove
tools.description: When a person asks: take a repo out of your bot, by name. Its checkout stays on disk; agents working in it are stopped. The chat gets a line the person can undo.

tools.name: project_setup
tools.description: Change your own bot when a person asks: title, icon or picture (an image in your working directory), color, shape, instructions (what its every agent is told; empty clears), setup (each new worktree's commands), env (plain variables; secrets via request_secret), archive.

archive.description: Its chat leaves the list and its lead stops.

commands.description: Each run with `sh -c` in the worktree.

tools.name: project_propose
tools.description: When a person asks for a new bot: propose its title and a GitHub repo to clone (url), or none. The chat shows them a card with what would be made; only their Approve makes it, as theirs. It waits for their answer and returns what was made, or that a clone started (you are woken when it ends); denied or unanswered, nothing is made.

url.description: A GitHub URL or owner/repo. Absent: a bot with no repo.

tools.name: project_message
tools.description: Text another bot's lead in its chat, as this bot's lead, when the work needs it: a question, a heads-up or an ask. Its reply wakes you. Returns a handle (N<n>); later wakes say when an order opened for it opens, closes, merges or fails. reply: the handle of a text you answer, only when the work needs an answer. Two bots trade at most 10 texts an hour. project: a title or bot id from factory_status.

tools.name: factory_status
tools.description: The other bots in one read, or the one named: each one's state (working, waiting on the person, blocked, idle), a red main, running agents, open orders, checklist not done, last merge and merges over 7 days, and this bot's asks to it with their orders. Read-only.

project.description: One bot, by title or bot id; absent, every bot but this one.

tools.name: chat_search
tools.description: Search all of your own chat for the messages holding every one of words (any order and case), optionally from and to a day (2026-10-20) or time, in UTC. Newest first, 20 a page, each with its id, time, author (human or lead: you) and its text around the words; before (a page's last id) reads the next. Read-only.

to.description: A day counts whole. Absent: now.

tools.name: chat_read
tools.description: Read the messages around one of your chat's, by its id from chat_search, oldest first: before and after say how many on each side (5 when absent, at most 10); both 0 reads that one whole. Read-only.

before.description: How many messages before it; absent, 5.

messageId.description: The message, by its id from chat_search.

tools.name: confirm_step
tools.description: Right before the final Confirm or Submit click on a site that doesn't pay or order (a booking, a cancellation, a form, a return, a post): site, the button's label, what clicking it does, the page's details and a chat_file screenshot. It goes through your approval mode like a send: once it returns, click that button, once; denied, don't. A payment, order or trade goes to the person with request_takeover.

does.description: In one or two plain sentences.

tools.name: usage_resume
tools.description: Lift the usage pause on your bot's machine and send every agent parked there "continue": only once its login has capacity again (the human says so, or a turn of yours just went through). At most once per 10 minutes per machine; a still-limited agent parks again.

machineId.description: The bot's machine; absent means it.

tools.name: change_enqueue
tools.description: Put a PR no task put there on its repo's merge train; only the train merges. after: PRs, in any repo, that must merge first; the train holds this one and tells you if one fails. A PR its review's findings block, enqueued again, gets a fresh full review of the same patch: for findings you resolved without a push.

after.description: Enqueuing a PR already on the train adds these, unless it is being merged.

tools.name: report
tools.description: Record your review verdict once, before your final message: the number of blocking and non-blocking findings and a summary of each. A finding is blocking only when it names what triggers it today and what breaks, or a miss against the brief; the rest is non-blocking. fleetd fills in your task and the head you reviewed.

tools.name: ask_lead
tools.description: Ask your lead a question. Carry on with what you can; the answer arrives as a message. If you can't go on without it, end your turn: the answer continues this thread. For a variable that is not set, name it and say why; never put a secret's value in the question.

tools.name: brief_read
tools.description: Read your workstream's brief, whole: its goal, why, pointers, constraints and done-when.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Write to one to five other agents of your bot by id (to: [T<n>]; `agents` lists them): an overlap, your PR's number, a finding they need. A running agent takes it at its next tool boundary. One that has finished but still waits (a wait_ci or Monitor of its own) is woken with it, its wait still armed; what else is sent to it within a few seconds goes in the same wake (woke). One that waits for an answer (its ask_lead question, or what it asked you and you now reply to), this continues (woke). One that finished waiting on nothing isn't restarted (not_woken): it gets it only if its lead continues it. Or post a note to the whole bot (to: ["bot"]): one line of at most 300 characters, a claim or finding on something shared outside your files ("moving the cloud pin in #404"). A note wakes nobody: every agent of the bot but reviews sees the newest at the top of `agents` while your task is live, a day at most; reviews post none. Product questions and scope go to your lead (ask_lead). Your lead and the person see every message.

to.description: The agents it is for (T<n>), 1 to 5, in the same bot; `agents` lists them. Or ["bot"] alone: a note to every agent of the bot.

tools.name: wait_ci
tools.description: Be woken when CI finishes: a GitHub Actions run, or the checks on a PR's current head. url is the run's (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>`; `gh run view <id> --json url -q .url`) or the PR's. Then end your turn: when it finishes, this thread continues with one line, the outcome and the failing jobs. With merged: true on a PR's URL, be woken when that PR merges instead, or if it fails on the merge train or is closed unmerged: one call per PR your next step builds on (a stacked PR, another writer's seam; `agents` gives its PR). Never end a turn saying you'll wait for a run or a merge without it, or ask your lead to ping you: nothing else wakes you.

merged.description:
A PR's only: wait for it to merge, not for its checks. Woken when it merges, when it fails on the merge train
(CI, review, refused) and when it is closed unmerged.

url.description: An Actions run's URL (`…/actions/runs/<id>`, anything after it ignored) or a PR's, in one of the bot's repos.

tools.name: review_read
tools.description: Read every finding of the latest reviews of your PRs in full, each with path:line, and people's GitHub reviews still open on them (people). pr (its URL or number) picks one; without it, a task reads its own PRs, a reviewer the PR it reviews, a lead its bot's PRs in the merge queue. A task may name any PR of its bot; another bot's are refused.

tools.name: chat_file
tools.description: Put a file you made in this bot's chat (a UI screenshot instead of a link, a PDF, a CSV, a document): path inside your working directory, at most 25 MiB, a png, jpeg, webp or gif, PDF, text, CSV, .docx, .xlsx, .pptx or .zip. Returns its attachmentId and the block that shows it: an image inline ({"v":1,"kind":"image","attachmentId":"F12","caption":"…"}), anything else a file card ({"v":1,"kind":"file","attachmentId":"F12"}). A task puts the id and its block kind in its result for its lead to show. Unshown, it is deleted after 24 h.

tools.name: publish_artifact
tools.description: Publish a report too long or rich for chat: Markdown (format md) or a whole HTML page (html). name: lowercase-hyphen words (sweep-report); title: what the human reads. Give content, or path (.html/.htm is html unless format says). The chat shows a card; the same name keeps a new version. Link it as `[Title](artifact:name)` or `artifact:name@2`. HTML is sandboxed offline: inline every script, style, font, image (data: URLs).

content.description: The whole document. Give this or path.

path.description: Relative to your working directory, or absolute.

tools.name: artifact_read
tools.description: Read a report published in this bot (publish_artifact), anyone's: its source as published, title, who published it and every version kept. name as in a link `artifact:sweep-report`; version as in `artifact:sweep-report@2`, else the newest. Past 64 KB it is cut, saying so. Another bot's are refused.

tools.name: attachment_read
tools.description: Save a file a person attached (a screenshot, a PDF, a document) in your own session, by its id (F12) as your brief or the chat names it, then open the path it returns with Read. It works wherever you run (a worktree, a hosted box), where a path into the lead's or another agent's folder does not. Another bot's are refused.

tools.name: session_start
tools.description: Open a browser session: a fresh Chrome with an empty profile, thrown away at session_end (a lead with no repo keeps its bot's profile and sign-ins), recorded. Drive it with the agent-browser CLI in Bash, already pointed at it: no --cdp, no browser of your own. purpose: one line on what for. kind android: a fresh Android 15 emulator, driven with agent-device (no --serial or --platform). kind linux_desktop: a fresh Linux desktop (1280x800, xterm), driven with desktop. kind mac: the agents' Mac's own screen, shared, driven with desktop and agent-desktop; it ends after 5 idle minutes. An iOS simulator runs on a Mac: `mac sim start` (mac --help); kind ios says how, or how to add a Mac.

tools.name: desktop
tools.description: Act on your Linux desktop session (session_start kind linux_desktop) or the agents' Mac's screen (kind mac). screenshot; left_click, right_click, middle_click, double_click, triple_click, mouse_move at coordinate [x, y] (screenshot pixels); left_click_drag from start_coordinate to coordinate; type text; key: xdotool names in text (Return, ctrl+s; cmd, option on the Mac); scroll by scroll_direction, scroll_amount; wait duration s; cursor_position; launch: text is a shell command run on the desktop in your working directory (the Mac: a session's folder). Mac only: agent_desktop runs one agent-desktop command, text its arguments (`snapshot --app Finder -i`; `skills get platform` first), via apps' accessibility refs, not the pointer; headless commands claim their app (one agent per app). Pointer, keys, launch and --headed take the Mac's lease (one agent at once). Screenshot after acting.

text.description: type: the text; key: the keys; launch: the command; agent_desktop: its arguments.

tools.name: session_end
tools.description: Close your browser session: the browser and its profile are thrown away (a kept project profile stays, with its sign-ins), and its recording goes to the hub.

tools.name: request_takeover
tools.description: Ask a person to take your browser over for what only they can do: a captcha, a login confirmation, a judgement call. reason: what they should do, in one line; they watch the page live. Carry on or end your turn: while they drive, agent-browser answers that a person has control; you are told when they hand it back, and the page is as they left it.

tools.name: fill_credential
tools.description: Fill a login field of your browser session from fleetd's vault without seeing the value: item (its label or id, from vault_items), field username, password or otp (a one-time code), target the field's CSS selector. It fills only on the item's own site, then submits the form; submit: false for a field before the last (a username before its password). From the first fill on, the session refuses reading values back. ref (op://<vault>/<item>/<field>) instead of item and field works for one release. Never ask anyone for a password: a login not in the vault, the person adds in Settings › Vault.

tools.name: fill_address
tools.description: Fill a vault address into your browser page's address form without seeing it: item (label or id; absent, the only one you may use, or Home), part shipping or billing when the form has both, target a CSS selector in the form when the page has several. It fills only at a checkout recorded with purchase_request, on the address's own sites, or a site the vault has a login for. Check the form after it; from then on the session refuses reading values back.

tools.name: vault_items
tools.description: The vault items your session may use: the workspace vault's logins (label, sites, fields present), addresses and cards (label only), and the variables already in your environment (their names). site narrows to a host's logins, kind to one kind. Never a value: fill with fill_credential, fill_address or purchase_fill.

oneOf.description: An environment variable for agents' sessions.

tools.name: vault_store
tools.description: Save a secret you hold as your bot's variable, out of the transcript: write it to a 0600 file in your worktree or TMPDIR, name it; it's sealed and stored, the file shredded; you get its fingerprint. Logged; no tool reads it back.

tools.name: vault_import_search
tools.description: Search the person's 1Password for logins, cards and addresses to import into fleetd's workspace vault: titles, kinds, vaults and sites, never a value. query matches a title or a site; kinds narrows. Then propose the ones needed with vault_import_propose.

oneOf.description: An environment variable for agents' sessions.

tools.name: vault_import_propose
tools.description: Propose importing 1Password items into fleetd's workspace vault: refs from vault_import_search, why one line. The chat shows an import card; the person ticks and taps Import, and fleetd reads the items sealed, so you never see them. Once imported, any bot's agents fill them from the vault.

tools.name: purchase_request
tools.description: Record a payment at the checkout open in your browser session, with the person's card, once basket and total are final: shop, total (`129.90`), currency (`EUR`) and items. Nobody is asked: it goes in the person's purchases log; then call purchase_fill. Never type card details. Trading, transfers and crypto are refused.

amount.description: In the total's currency, when shown.

domain.description: The checkout page's host: the card fills only there and in its payment frames.

tools.name: purchase_fill
tools.description: Fill a purchase's card into the checkout's card fields (the shop's page and its payment provider's frames) without seeing it: requestId from purchase_request, on that checkout with its card form showing, within 15 minutes. It fills once and the chat says what was paid; then check the total and click Pay yourself. A bank's confirmation (3-D Secure, a code) goes to the person with request_takeover. From then on the session refuses reading values back.

tools.name: request_secure_input
tools.description: When a page needs something only the person may give and you must never see (an ID number, a texted code): site, target (the field's CSS selector, in the page or a frame), label in their words ("Passport number"), why in one line. They type it in a sealed field and fleetd fills it; you are woken once it is in. With ref nobody is asked: call secure_input_fill. Never ask for such a value in chat.

ref.description: A field of an Identity, Passport, Driver License or Social Security item in their 1Password to fill from.

domain.description: The page's host: it fills only there.

tools.name: secure_input_fill
tools.description: Fill a secure input from 1Password into its field: requestId from request_secure_input, on that page within 15 minutes. It fills once; from then on the session refuses reading values back.

tools.name: request_sign_in
tools.description: When a sign-in page needs a login you don't have: site, the CSS selector of each field the page shows now (username, password, otp), why in one line. A vault login for the site fills at once and submits, with no ask. Else the person gets a secure sign-in form in the chat (saved to the vault by default), fleetd fills the fields and submits, and you are woken; you never see the values. If the page then asks for a one-time code, call it again with otp. Never ask for a login or code in chat; request_takeover only for captchas, passkeys, device approvals or judgement calls.

otp.description: The one-time code field's CSS selector.

domain.description: The page's host: it fills only there.

username.description: The username or email field's CSS selector.
